title: Solar Panels: What to Know and What They Pay
desc: What to check before you buy rooftop solar, and every open solar rebate we track, with the official page and the date we checked each one.
lead: Rooftop solar makes electricity from sunlight. Here is what to check before you buy, and which programs pay today.
image_alt: Solar panels on a tiled house roof
intro:
Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity for your home. How much you save depends on your roof, your shade, your electricity rates and the rules for sending extra power back to the grid.

The rebate rules can matter as much as the panels. Some programs need approval before you buy. Some do not accept systems that sell power under a net metering agreement. Many need a licensed contractor. Read the rules for your utility first, then compare quotes.
checks: Approval first. Some programs want written approval before you buy. Buying first can cost you the rebate.
How the system connects. Some programs do not accept systems under a net metering agreement. Ask your installer how yours is set up.
A licensed contractor. Many programs need one, and some also need a program-registered company.
Your roof. Ask for a shade check and the roof age. A roof that needs work soon changes the math.
The quote. Compare at least three. Look at panel brand, system size and what is included.
faq: Do I need a battery with solar?
No. A battery is a separate choice. Some programs pay for a battery only when it goes in with new solar.
Is solar worth it for every home?
No. It depends on your roof, shade and rates. We tell homeowners when the math does not work.
Can renters get a solar rebate?
Program rules differ. Most are written for owners, so check the official page.
How do I know the rebate is real?
Each program in the table links to its official page, and shows the date we last checked it.

extra:
Questions to ask before you sign

Ask each installer how big the system is and what it is meant to cover: part of your bill or all of it. Ask what happens to extra power you do not use, because the answer changes both the rebate rules and your savings. Ask who handles the approvals with your utility, and how long that usually takes.

Ask what the warranty covers for the panels, the inverter and the roof work, and who you call if something stops working. Get the answers in writing, and compare three quotes line by line.

If a company pushes you to sign the same day, take that as a reason to slow down. A good installer will give you time to read the program rules.
